Keep it nearby

A one-page dog-reading cheat sheet.

Scan the whole dog, add context, and choose the kindest next step.

Open body map
Whole-dog scan

What is changing right now?

One signal can be ambiguous. Look for a cluster, compare it with your dog’s baseline, and notice whether they can move away.

EyesSoft blinking is different from a hard stare, darting eyes, or showing the whites.
EarsPosition can show interest or worry; include the rest of the body and the dog’s natural ear shape.
MouthLoose and relaxed is different from a tight mouth, lip lick, yawn, or repeated panting.
BodyLoose curves and weight shifts tell a different story from freezing, leaning away, or stiffness.
TailHeight, speed, width, and stiffness matter together. A wag is not a universal “yes.”
MovementWatch speed, direction, pauses, recovery, and whether the dog can disengage.
ContextAsk what happened before, who is nearby, what the dog wants, and whether there is an exit.
ChoiceThe clearest clue is whether your dog can choose to approach, move away, sniff, eat, or rest.

If the dog asks for space

  1. Pause reaching, hugging, cornering, or asking for more.
  2. Turn sideways and open a clear exit with more distance.
  3. Watch for softening; if signals escalate, separate safely and seek qualified help.
WagSignals ✦

Educational guidance, not a diagnosis. Every dog is an individual; breed, health, age, history, and context all matter.
